- EVERY READER OF THE DEFENDER'S DECLARED CHAIN TAKES ONE LINK HEAD (ASK 424; Shared Library chain_count, drvLinks and drvChainOf in engine and child; declared() and dlinks() in Build Synthesis, Build Independent Verdict, Build Save Body, Panel Build, Format Markdown, D4 Build, D4 Extract, C4 Build, C4 Extract, C4G Extract, D4B Extract and C4B Extract; cecDeclared() and cecDlinks() in Close Enforcer Build, Judge Contradiction Build and Judge Contradiction Record):
    - Why: runs 27665, 38661, 39015 and 39266 wrote their chains "D1:" to "Dn:". chain_count read 0, so k2Marks walked no link; drvLinks gave no list to drvUnlink; drvChainOf told the judges "DEFENDER CHAIN: not found in the prompt"; cecDeclared gave no links to the close-contradiction check. declared() keeps at most 3 non-blank lines before its first numbered line, so it returned the heading and D1 to D3: the round 4 prompts (D4 Build "YOUR DECLARED CHAIN -- ... copied verbatim by the system", and C4 Build) showed the chain without its conclusion link, and dlinks() gave the close-round numbering check no declared list.
    - What it does: the five readers take one link head. R2 to R5 (drvLinks, drvChainOf's defender branch, cecDeclared and cecDlinks, declared and dlinks) read `^\s*(?:#+\s*)?[*_]*\s*D?([0-9]+)[*_]*(?:[.:)](?![0-9])|\s+[dash]{1,3}(?:\s|$))`, case-insensitive, where [dash] is the hyphen and the Unicode dashes; chain_count takes the same head without the leading `^\s*`, as the ASK 423 bound reader does; spaces still pass through its `[*_]*\s*`, so it too reads an indented chain. "D1:", "D1.", "**1.**", "### 3)", "4 -- d" and "D12:" are heads; "28:10 For precept", "1.5 x" and "2 Corinthians 5:17" are not. Each reader keeps its own start, continuation, stop and output rules. The copies stay one text each (12 declared, 10 dlinks, 3 cecDeclared, 3 cecDlinks), and the library change is the same in the engine and the child.
    - Shown offline, over the 245 stored chains: where today's reader held a numbered link the new output is equal (chain_count 241 of 241; the other four readers 229 of 229 each). chain_count newly reads exactly the 4 runs (6, 5, 4 and 5 links); the other four readers newly read 16 runs each, the 4 and 12 older runs written with "D1" and a dash, "D1." or "**1.**" heads, each to its conclusion link. For 39266, D4 Build's declared() gave the heading and D1 to D3 before and D1 to D5 after. Planted: an indented "  1." chain is read alike by all five (3 links); a "28:10" line after "D2:" is not a head.
    - Stored rows are not recomputed. Through chain_count and drvLinks no stored count, conceded-link figure or standing of the 4 runs changes (their round 3 conceded and narrowed no link). drvChainOf, cecDeclared and declared changed only what models and enforcers were shown; that effect cannot be measured from the record. Which code version ran the older runs was not checked.
